title: Calculation and Visualization
description: Learn a reliable thinking process: identify candidate moves, calculate forcing lines first, and visualize the resulting positions before committing.

sections.title: Candidate Moves
sections.content: Strong calculation starts by listing candidate moves — the two or three most promising options. Then calculate the most forcing ones first: checks, captures, and threats, since they limit the opponent's replies.

positions.commentary: Identify your candidate moves, then calculate the most forcing options first. Forcing moves are easier to calculate because replies are limited.

sections.title: Calculate to a Quiet Position
sections.content: Don't stop a calculation in the middle of a tactical sequence. Follow each line until the position quiets down, then evaluate. And always do a final blunder-check before you play the move.

positions.commentary: Calculate forcing lines to their end, then evaluate the resulting position. A move that wins material but loses the king is no good — always blunder-check.
hints: Follow lines to a quiet point
Evaluate the end position, not the middle

exercises.title: Forced Recapture
exercises.description: Black to play. The bishop just captured on f7 with check — find the only legal, forcing reply.
